correctness.rationale: With n≥2 and a,b>0, differentiation of the Bernstein basis gives an L∞-dual signed kernel: n times a convex mixture of adjacent beta density differences. Each beta difference crosses only at c=(a+k)/(n+a+b−1) and has L1 norm 2V(k). Strict convexity of h(t)=t log t−log Γ(t+1), from 1/t−ψ1(t+1)>0, forces its discrete maximum to the outer k=0 or n−1 endpoint, larger at x=0 iff a<b. Pointwise derivative norms attain the bound at the selected endpoint with the sign of its signed beta kernel. For n≥3 interior Bernstein weights make the bound strict; for n=2,a=b, distinct crossings yield strict L1 triangle inequality. Gamma-ratio limits yield 2n(n/(n+1))^n in the uniform case and the claimed fixed-(a,b) coefficient. Independent incomplete-beta CDF computations reproduced 243 adjacent variations for integer parameters.
residual_risks: Bounded independent calculations are not substitutes for all quantified analytical steps; no formal proof or external attestation is asserted.
